pharm: Laxative for constipation; bowel preparation (higher-volume PEG-electrolyte solutions)
quick: 17 g powder dissolved in 240 mL liquid once daily
Dissolve in water/juice; with or without food
Considered low risk (minimal absorption); use if needed
Bowel response; electrolytes with prolonged/high-dose use
summary: Polyethylene glycol 3350 is an osmotic laxative that retains water in the stool to soften it and promote a bowel movement, typically within 1-3 days. The usual OTC adult dose is 17 g dissolved in about 240 mL of liquid once daily for up to about 7 days. It is essentially non-absorbed and well tolerated. Higher-volume PEG-electrolyte solutions are used for bowel preparation. It should be avoided if bowel obstruction is suspected.
indications: Treatment of chronic constipation (under medical advice)

dosage.d: 17 g (about 1 heaping tablespoon) dissolved in 240 mL of liquid, once daily
dosage.n: Use no more than 7 days unless advised by a clinician

dosage.d: 17 g daily; titrate per response under medical supervision
PEG-electrolyte solution per product instructions (e.g. 4 L split-dose)

admin: Dissolve the measured powder fully in about 240 mL (8 oz) of water, juice, or other beverage
May be taken with or without food
Allow 1-3 days for a bowel movement
For bowel prep, follow the specific PEG-electrolyte product instructions
moa: Polyethylene glycol 3350 is a high-molecular-weight, osmotically active, poorly absorbed polymer. It binds and retains water within the intestinal lumen, increasing stool water content and volume. This softens the stool and increases bowel distension, stimulating peristalsis and producing a laxative effect without net electrolyte loss.

absolute: Known or suspected bowel obstruction or perforation
relative: Severe inflammatory bowel disease (e.g. toxic colitis, megacolon)
Symptoms of appendicitis or acute abdomen
monitor: Bowel function and resolution of constipation
Serum electrolytes with prolonged, high-dose or bowel-prep use
Signs of obstruction (severe pain, vomiting, distension)

preg: Polyethylene glycol 3350 is minimally absorbed systemically and is generally considered low risk in pregnancy; it is commonly used for constipation when dietary measures are insufficient.
lact: Because of negligible systemic absorption, PEG 3350 is considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is required for the standard laxative dose, as PEG 3350 is not significantly absorbed. With large-volume bowel-prep solutions, monitor fluid and electrolyte balance, particularly in renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is required.

moderate: Other oral medicines around bowel-prep - large-volume PEG may reduce absorption of drugs taken near the prep
minor: Generally minimal interactions due to non-absorption
interactions.food: Can be taken with or without food; dissolve in any beverage.
interactions.diagnostics: High-volume bowel-prep use may cause transient electrolyte shifts; routine laxative use rarely affects tests.

serious: Severe or persistent diarrhoea with dehydration and electrolyte disturbance
emergency: Severe dehydration with electrolyte imbalance (e.g. with excessive use)

monitoring: Resolution of constipation and stool frequency/consistency
Electrolytes and hydration if used at high dose, for prolonged periods, or for bowel prep
Watch for signs of obstruction (severe pain, vomiting)
counsel: Dissolve the dose fully in a full glass of liquid and drink it all
It may take 1 to 3 days to work
Do not use for more than 7 days for occasional constipation unless advised
Stop and seek advice if you have severe stomach pain, rectal bleeding, or no bowel movement after use
Drink adequate fluids and consider more dietary fibre
pk: Not applicable (acts locally in the gut)
Not applicable; minimally absorbed and excreted unchanged
Effect persists while taken; reversible on stopping
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); keep container closed
pearls: Osmotic, non-stimulant laxative that retains water in stool - generally well tolerated for routine and chronic constipation
Does not cause significant electrolyte loss at usual doses, unlike some other laxatives
Avoid if bowel obstruction is suspected
Effect is gradual (1-3 days) - not for immediate relief
Distinct from large-volume PEG-electrolyte solutions used for colonoscopy preparation
missed: If a daily dose is missed, take it when remembered; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it and resume the usual once-daily schedule. Do not take extra to catch up.
overdose: Excessive use can cause severe diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dehydration and electrolyte imbalance. Manage by stopping the laxative and replacing fluids and electrolytes; severe cases need supportive care.
